10   invocation will be offered by Rabbi Shmuel 

11   Butman of the Lubavitch Youth Organization in

13                Rabbi?

14                RABBI BUTMAN:   {in Hebrew}  Our 

15   heavenly Father, we ask You to bestow Your 

16   blessings upon the members of the New York State 

17   Senate and their families.  Bless them with good 

18   health, long life and success in all of their 

19   endeavors.  

20                We are here offering this prayer as 

21   we are now celebrating the 113th birthday of the 

22   Lubavitcher Rebbe, Rabbi Menachem M. Schneerson.  

23                The Rebbe worried for education of 

24   all children.  This was his prime goal, 

25   education of all children of the world.  The 


                                                                1140

 1   Rebbe said many times that he wants a child to 

 2   know, every child of the world, that there is an 

 3   Eye that sees and there is an Ear that hears and 

 4   that the world is not a jungle.  And when the 

 5   Rebbe spoke education, he spoke education about 

 6   all the children of the world.

 7                I remember in 1991 I opened the 

 8   United States Senate in Washington.  Before that, 

 9   I went to see the Rebbe.  And the Rebbe said that 

10   "You should take with you a pushkeh" -- a pushkeh 

11   is a tzedakah box -- "and when you are offering a 

12   prayer, you should also put a dollar bill into 

13   the pushkeh.  And that everybody should know what 

14   you are doing, and everybody should see what you 

15   are doing, and let them know what money has to be 

16   used for."

17                Well, we are going to do the same 

18   now.  We are going to put in a dollar.  On the 

19   dollar it says "In God We Trust," and you just 

20   said that before.  And we're going to offer it as 

21   an offering in the pushkeh.  And we're going to 

22   ask you, and everyone who wants, to participate.  

23                Friends, I don't want you to accept 

24   this that this is a fundraising campaign.  

25   Because if this would be a fundraising campaign, 


                                                                1141

 1   we would ask you for much more than one dollar.

 2                (Laughter.)

 3                RABBI BUTMAN:   This is, however, a 

 4   campaign, as the Rebbe says, to do more goodness 

 5   and kindness.

 6                King David says, in Psalm 113 -- 

 7   it's 113 years of the Rebbe, and this is 

 8   Psalm 113.  In Psalm 113, King David says that 

 9   Almighty God listens to everyone.  He listens to 

10   the poor, and He elevates him from the depths to 

11   sit together with the princes of his nation.  And 

12   He transforms a childless woman into a happy 

13   mother.  This is the power, this is the power of 

14   prayer.

15                I want you to know that every 

16   Sabbath, every Shabbos, we say a special prayer 

17   for each and every single one of you.  We say it 

18   in our synagogues, and we say the {in Hebrew}.  

19   Which means all of those who serve the public 

20   faithfully, as you do, we ask for Almighty God to 

21   give you all the blessings that you need in your 

22   private life and in your communal life.  

23                So we hope that all the blessings 

24   will be bestowed upon you, and may you pass the 

25   budget successfully before Passover.

                                                                1146

 1   roll.

 3                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

 4   Kennedy to explain his vote.

 5                SENATOR KENNEDY:   Thank you very 

 6   much, Mr. President.

 7                I'm a proud cosponsor of this Alix's 

 8   Law.  I would like to give credit where credit is 

 9   due, and the prime sponsor from Western New York, 

10   Senator Gallivan, has been a tremendous champion 

11   of this initiative over the course of the last 

12   several years.  

13                It's named Alix's Law in memory of a 

14   young woman whose life was tragically lost in 

15   Western New York when she was hit by a motor 

16   vehicle that continued on.  And in this 

17   hit-and-run accident, she tragically lost her 

18   life.  This is in response to that horrific 

19   incident.  

20                But far too many lives have been 

21   lost across this state and across this nation due 

22   to individuals that have gotten behind the wheel 

23   of a vehicle impaired by alcohol or drugs, have 

24   hit an individual, and have left the scene of an 

25   accident.  


                                                                1147

 1                This is a common-sense reform that 

 2   if in fact a driver is intoxicated, gets into an 

 3   accident, flees the scene of an accident, that 

 4   individual will be presumed to have known that 

 5   they caused damage to either property or to an 

 6   individual.

 7                It shouldn't be the burden of a 

 8   prosecution to prove whether or not a driver 

 9   under the influence knew whether or not they hit 

10   an individual or property when they fled the 

11   scene of an accident.  This is a crime on top of 

12   the crime of driving while intoxicated to begin 

13   with.

14                In other words, life sentences for 

15   victims have been a thing of the past, while 

16   drivers that have been intoxicated attempt to 

17   skirt the law and escape justice while leaving 

18   the scene of an accident.  This will close the 

19   loophole in the law, and it will hold individuals 

20   accountable.

21                This bill closes the loophole, and I 

22   want to thank all of my colleagues from Western 

23   New York that have helped to champion this 

24   cause -- in memory, again, of young Alix Rice.

25                Mr. President, I vote aye.

20                SENATOR SEWARD:   Yes, thank you, 

21   Mr. President, to explain my vote.  

22                This legislation before us creates a 

23   new crime of staging a motor vehicle accident 

24   which would be punishable as a felony offense.  

25                You know, staging an accident is 


                                                                1152

 1   defined as intentionally causing a collision for 

 2   the purpose of committing insurance fraud by 

 3   inappropriately and illegally collecting no-fault 

 4   benefits.

 5                Now, this bill is referred to as 

 6   Alice's Law.  It's named after Alice Ross, who 

 7   was a 71-year-old grandmother who was killed as a 

 8   result of one of these staged accidents in the 

 9   Borough of Queens.  Mrs. Ross was on her way to 

10   visit her daughter at her daughter's house when 

11   she was intentionally struck from behind by a 

12   vehicle that was carrying three men who were out 

13   looking for an unsuspecting victim.  The impact 

14   of this accident caused Mrs. Ross's vehicle to go 

15   off the road and hit a tree, causing her death.

16                After the accident, these three 

17   perpetrators then went off to one of these 

18   medical mills and feigned an assortment of 

19   injuries in order to collect phony no-fault 

20   benefits.

21                You know, criminals who stage these 

22   auto accidents endanger the lives of innocent 

23   people and also drive up insurance premiums for 

24   every single New Yorker.  The perpetrators commit 

25   these crimes having a total disregard for public 


                                                                1153

 1   safety, and they're only out to make a fast buck.

 2                You know, innocent people should not 

 3   be made pawns in these sometimes deadly schemes.  

 4   So this bill will not only help contain no-fault 

 5   fraud and reduce insurance premiums but also make 

 6   our highways safer.  

 7                Mr. President, I vote aye.

 9   Seward to be recorded in the affirmative.

15                This bill would amend Section 473 of 

16   the Laws of 2010 which amended the Racing, 

17   Pari-Mutuel Wagering and Breeding Law related to 

18   our state Thoroughbred Breeding and Development 

19   Fund.

20                This section of the law is scheduled 

21   to sunset on October 28, 2015.  We would like it 

22   extended another year.  And let me tell you what 

23   the fund does.

24                First of all, payments are made to 

25   the fund on a quarterly basis.  The percentage of 


                                                                1159

 1   revenue that can be allocated to breeder awards 

 2   would be maintained at 65 percent, which is what 

 3   it has been, and the amount of money used for 

 4   promoting the breeding and raising of 

 5   thoroughbred horses would remain the same, and 

 6   there would be administrative allotments of 

 7   6 percent.

 8                Now, where does the money come from?  

 9   It comes from 1.5 percent of the amount wagered 

10   for regular, multiple and exotic wagers on 

11   thoroughbred horse racing, and 3 percent of the 

12   amount wagered on superexotic wagers -- betting 

13   on six or more horses in a single bet -- and, 

14   additionally, 1 percent of the net win from 

15   Resorts World Casino at Aqueduct and 1.25 percent 

16   of the net win from the racino at Finger Lakes.

17                What these monies do, they support 

18   the breeding industry in the State of New York.

19                This was approved unanimously by our 

20   Racing Committee.  It was approved last year, the 

21   extender, 60 to 0.  And it comes up again to give 

22   them another year.

24   because of the racing industry, and this enables 

25   the breeders to keep their breeding industry
